items.summary: A single-sentence cartoon caption attributes a warning about dangerous technology innovations to Steve Jones, without further context or explanation of the subject's remarks. The item offers no figures, sources, or supporting detail beyond this one line.
items.title: Steve Jones Cartoon Warns Against Risky Technology Advances

items.summary: A company behind a large AI development near Glasgow has said the scheme will be fully served by the National Grid, revising an earlier pledge to draw 1GW from green sources. The Guardian prompted the change after questioning the commitment. DataVita says its grid supply would come through a renewable power purchase agreement and that solar and windfarms could connect later. It remains eligible for £202m in public wealth guarantees while planning a 500MW datacentre expected to create 3,400 jobs.
items.title: DataVita abandons renewable promise for Glasgow AI datacentre

items.summary: Caregivers face a growing crisis as an estimated 63 million Americans cared for someone with a medical condition or disability in 2025, spending up to 27 hours per week on care. New caregiver apps are emerging to help manage medications, appointments, and communication between family members. Developers like Bret Koncak of Mejo and Nasha Fitter of Citizen Health aim to reduce the mental load by consolidating medical information and offering AI assistance. However, experts caution that most of these tools are not FDA-reviewed medical devices, their safety remains uncertain, and health data may fall outside HIPAA protections. One expert noted the solution requires collaboration across government, private sector, and families.
items.title: AI Caregiver Apps Promise Relief Amid Growing Burden

items.summary: The article asks why some people get a lot from artificial intelligence while others struggle, and answers that the difference comes down largely to how you use it rather than the technology itself. It warns against offloading thinking to chatbots, which can dull creativity and create dependence on an imperfect tool, but suggests using AI to challenge yourself, stress-test your work, and outsource routine tasks may feel like a significant upgrade. The piece then offers tips for making these platforms work better.
items.title: Five tips for getting more out of AI

items.summary: A security check called a CAPTCHA normally confirms visitors are human, but scammers now abuse it to install malicious software on Macs and PCs. Fake pop-ups mimic trusted sites like Amazon.com or Facebook.com and ask users to press keyboard shortcuts such as Windows+R then Ctrl+V, which copies hidden code onto their clipboard so attackers can download programs that steal data. The Federal Trade Commission released an alert earlier this year warning consumers of the tactic.
items.title: Scammers Turn Familiar Security Check Into Data-Stealing Trap

items.summary: Researchers document that dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes have expanded across Nepal, reaching elevations up to 2,500 meters (8,200 feet) over the past decade. According to a January literature review in Clinical Infection in Practice, transmission has grown from localized outbreaks since first appearing in 2004 into major nationwide epidemics through 2019, 2022 and 2023. Local media report the virus reached 76 out of the country's 77 districts with roughly 9,000 recorded infections and at least six deaths in 2025 alone. Sunita Baral of Nepal Health Research Council notes dengue was once confined to lowland Terai regions but now appears in Kathmandu. Rising temperatures let mosquitoes survive higher altitudes while urban water storage creates breeding grounds. Erin Mordecai of Stanford University says global dengue burdens have risen roughly 18 percent over historical baselines, hitting cooler highlands hardest.
items.title: Dengue Fever Spreads Higher in Nepal's Warming Himalayas

items.summary: Inside Climate News, via its partner Living on Earth, reports an interview with U.S. Rep. Jared Huffman, who is in line to chair the House Energy and Natural Resources Committee as Democrats take control. Huffman outlines a two-part agenda: oversight and investigations into matters like mineral deals involving Trump inner-circle financial interests and the Freedom 250 entity’s reprogrammed funds, plus an affirmative policy push he says must not be constrained by Donald Trump’s laws or permits. He cites rising utility bills and offshore wind cancellations as election drivers and flags a bipartisan Great American Outdoors Act 250 bill that Huffman hopes to advance in the lame duck session. Huffman notes subpoena power may come “sometime in January” and warns of two months of chaotic negotiations before the next Congress seats.
items.title: Huffman Vows Reset of Natural Resources Committee Agenda

items.summary: Electric truck maker Harbinger raised $240 million in its latest Series D round, co-led by Tiger Global, the Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. The company says it will use the money to expand energy storage systems, power generation, autonomy software, defense applications, and medium-duty manufacturing capacity. Since 2021, Harbinger has raised over $650 million total. Co-Founder and CEO John Harris said electrification is central to its mission of reinventing critical systems.
items.title: Harbinger Secures $240 Million in Series D Funding Round

items.summary: Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter range with the XENTER E, a high-wheel 16-inch model aimed at European city riding. It uses Yamaha's new eAxle powertrain producing 7.5 kW of peak power and places it in Europe's A1 license category. Powered by a 3.5 kWh battery claiming 108 km on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, early reports point to €7,799 in Germany, with deliveries expected from spring 2027.
items.title: Yamaha Unveils High-Wheel Electric Scooter Targeting European Commuters

items.summary: U.S. solar equipment inventories expanded by 126% during the second quarter of 2026 as project developers accelerated procurement ahead of federal trade cutoffs, including a July construction-start deadline and Dec. 4 measures affecting polysilicon, wafers, cells, and modules. OCI Energy CEO Sabah Bayatli said uncertainty over minimum import price thresholds—$0.22 per watt for cells and $0.38 per watt for finished modules—makes pricing difficult post-December. Developers are restructuring multi-party contracts to share tariff risk rather than speculating on spot prices, with costs ultimately flowing into higher power purchase agreement pricing.
items.title: U.S. solar developers brace for Section 232 tariff deadline

items.summary: Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) explored how diverse teams can improve decisions during six Solar & Storage Live events across the UK, Spain, Switzerland, Italy and France this year. The article reports that trust, participation and leadership enable people to challenge assumptions, shape outcomes and take ownership without senior titles. Quotes from Carmen Madrid of Women in Solar+ Europe, Jessimiela Usidame, Kim Keats Martínez, Filipa Monteiro Martins, Hollie Carek and Nadia Lalout-Landemaine support the argument. The piece notes that silence locks in risk and cost, and calls for everyday inclusive practices ahead of a WiSEu Breakfast Workshop on 25 November during Genera in Madrid.
items.title: How the Solar+ industries can make better decisions for the energy transition

items.summary: Rail minister Peter Hendy told a London industry conference this week that the legislation creating Great British Railways had “a fair chance of getting royal assent” before parliament’s winter break, potentially wrapping up its establishment in law by Christmas. The new arm’s-length body would bring track and train services under one control. Speakers acknowledged substantial challenges: network manager Network Rail cited two derailments within 24 hours amid a summer of delays, while the regulator Office of Rail and Road noted renewal spending had fallen from nearly £5bn to less than £4bn over five years. Some critics warned that future funding could remain uncertain under different governments.
items.title: Great British Railways law may pass by Christmas amid old problems

items.summary: German chancellor Friedrich Merz, Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten and four other European leaders wrote to Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa urging the UK’s return to the EU internal electricity market ahead of a 20 November summit. They argue integration would unlock North Sea clean energy and lower costs for British consumers. Officials warn it could be controversial, as the UK might contribute to cohesion funds.
items.title: Five European leaders urge closer EU-UK energy ties

items.summary: Researchers using Chile's Very Large Telescope spotted a white dwarf, J1328−1450 in Virgo about 1,600 light-years away, whose debris disc forms two distinct rings rather than the single disc seen in the 21 similar systems previously found. Astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches said the configuration suggests planetary remnants can survive a star's transformation and may mirror our own solar system billions of years from now.
items.title: Astronomers Spot White Dwarf With Two Rings of Planetary Debris

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings on Saturday, describing the festival as symbolising India's determination to overcome darkness. He reaffirmed his annual tradition of celebrating with armed forces personnel, a practice he has followed for years. In a video message shared on X, he wished citizens happiness, peace and prosperity, while also greeting Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan earlier that day.
items.title: PM Modi Extends Diwali Greetings and Vows to Continue Tradition With Soldiers

items.summary: A reference lists Diwali 2026 as falling on Sunday, November 8. Citing Drik Panchang, it gives the New Delhi Lakshmi Puja muhurat from 5:54 PM to 7:50 PM, an auspicious window of about one hour and 56 minutes during Vrishabha Kaal. The timings may vary across cities depending on local sunset and Panchang calculations.
items.title: Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Timings Listed for Major Indian Cities

items.summary: A report by Cease in the UK and Collective Shout in Australia accuses TikTok of helping promote and normalise the sex industry, according to a report. Researchers studied non-explicit posts over a year from some OnlyFans’ most popular young female performers, finding coded references hidden inside lifestyle content about shopping, pets or skincare. Performers reportedly used euphemisms like “corn” for porn or emoji combinations to evade blocks while hinting their adult content is available elsewhere. The report’s authors called for extending bans on explicit material shown to under-18s to include such promotional posts. Melinda Tankard Reist of Collective Shout condemned TikTok as an industrial-scale digital pimp grooming young women into producing explicit content, though the platform and OnlyFans both denied facilitating minors’ access.
items.title: Campaigners accuse TikTok of funneling girls into sex work

items.summary: Engineers tested the world's first 4,000-meter-class airborne wind power system over Yueyang in central China on November 6. The China-made S4000 uses a helium-filled platform to lift power modules up to 4,000 meters and transmit electricity via tether cable. Officials say urban testing assesses safe operation near populated areas as cities become key deployment targets for high-altitude wind energy.
items.title: China Tests World's First High-Altitude Floating Wind Power System Over City

items.summary: At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit's forum on the Development of Internet Public Welfare, CGTN spoke with Chinese actor Yue Man-lok. He has sponsored children in rural China for years and described how the internet transformed charitable giving: supporting a cause no longer requires being there in person. "It's about how much you want to help," he said.
items.title: Yue Man-lok on How Internet Simplifies Charity Giving

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies. He reported 12 regions came under attack with Kyiv hit hardest, nine people hurt including one child, and strikes on substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear power plants to Kyiv.
items.title: Zelensky Reports Widespread Damage After Russian Strikes on Ukraine's Power Grid

items.summary: Two teenagers were arrested overnight and on Saturday morning after a suspected sword attack near St Peter's high school in Tuffley, Gloucester. A 17-year-old was reported with a superficial wound believed to have been caused by the sword; another 17-year-old boy was not physically injured. Officers responded shortly after 8.50am on Friday and armed police searched for suspects while schools were put on lockdown.
items.title: Two men arrested after boy injured in Gloucester sword attack

items.summary: As ballots from Tuesday's US midterm elections are still being counted, analysts pivot attention to the upcoming 2028 presidential contest. The article offers four takeaways: midterms winners now carry momentum, with Democrats buoyed by congressional gains; however, a strong showing does not guarantee victory two years later, as Barack Obama won in 2012 despite Republican midterm surges. Leadership figures like JD Vance and Marco Rubio face pressure amid voter anger over the administration, while left- and moderate-wing Democrats compete for influence. Hispanic voters' support must be actively earned by both parties as traditional strongholds shift.
items.title: Four Takeaways on the Shifting 2028 White House Race

items.summary: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi took pole position for the Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday, Nov 7, smashing the lap record twice at Lusail. He clocked one minute 50.028 seconds, finishing 0.266 seconds ahead of championship leader Marc Marquez. Qualifying left only 18 riders on the grid after Yamaha teams withdrew over travel restrictions.
items.title: Bezzecchi smashes lap record twice to grab Qatar MotoGP pole from Marquez

items.summary: Moscow launched a massive overnight strike on Kyiv while Ukraine prepares for talks with Russia and the United States next week. At least five people were injured, and Russian missiles damaged buildings, closed a bridge over the Dnipro River, and caused power and water outages.
items.title: Russia Launches Massive Overnight Strike on Kyiv as Talks Loom

items.summary: After retiring from professional tennis in October, ending a 22-year career, Gael Monfils has become the captain of France's Davis Cup team, the French Tennis Federation (FFT) announced on Saturday. He took over the non-playing role from Paul-Henri Mathieu and is set to support France as they begin their qualifying campaign in February.
items.title: Gael Monfils becomes captain of France's Davis Cup team

items.summary: Sun coral, an invasive Indo-Pacific species first seen in Brazil in the 1980s, is spreading along roughly 3,500 kilometers (2,175 miles) of coastline. Estimates suggest it can expand at a rate of 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) per year and may alter reefs once it covers 45% of rocky substrate. In 2018 Brazil launched a National Plan to prevent, control and monitor the invasion. Marine biologist Adriana Gomes leads volunteer divers removing colonies near Cagarras Islands off Ipanema Beach.
items.title: Brazil Divers Remove Invasive Sun Coral Along Coastal Reefs

items.summary: Mongabay reporter Max Radwin investigated illegal gold mining advancing on Indigenous Wayana communities in Suriname's Amazon, near the French Guiana border. Miners are clearing forest and polluting rivers with mercury despite a government pledge to combat the activity. The report directs readers to Mongabay's full story for more of his findings.
items.title: Illegal Gold Mining Expands Across Suriname's Indigenous Amazon Territory

items.summary: The company behind the under-construction Brenner Base Tunnel project, a 55 km rail link between Innsbruck in Austria and Fortezza in Italy, confirmed it had been hit by a cyberattack on 17 October after activating its security protocols. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said he was targeted over Italy's support for Ukraine, with criminals sharing his personal data online; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed her support. Initial investigations point to the pro-Russian group Everest, per Tiroler Tageszeitung.
items.title: Italian Foreign Minister and Tunnel Firm Hit by Cyberattacks

items.summary: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian air defence systems in southern Iran, targeting an anti-aircraft device on Qeshm Island. President Donald Trump called them “minor strikes,” saying the system was knocked out in about 15 minutes, maybe five, while insisting progress continues with Qatar’s mediation. Iranian state media reported two missiles hit Suza without identifying targets or damage; locals posted explosions online. The IRGC claimed to shoot down a US drone, which Washington did not confirm. Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals but remains unwilling to negotiate until core conditions are met: ending the port blockade, lifting sanctions, unfreezing assets and compensation. Diplomats across the Gulf stressed talks continue amid fears of an all-out war.
items.title: US Strikes Iranian Air Defenses as Diplomacy Continues

items.summary: The 2026 Global Mayors Dialogue opened in Ningbo on China's east coast, drawing mayors and representatives from 20 cities across 15 countries and regions. Participants discussed sustainable development through port trade cooperation, smart manufacturing, and urban governance. The event is organized by the host city as part of an international exchange among municipal leaders.
items.title: Mayors Gather in Ningbo for Global Dialogue

items.summary: Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of China's National People's Congress, met separately with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema and Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Zhao pledged to strengthen bilateral relations and expand cooperation with both countries, while each leader expressed hope for deeper legislative exchanges and closer ties.
items.title: China's top legislator meets Gabonese and Austrian leaders in Beijing

items.summary: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned Saturday that heavy rains have flooded shelters in the Gaza Strip, placing displaced families at 'immediate risk.' OCHA said most of Gaza's 2.1 million residents remain displaced and living in deteriorating tents with limited protection against worsening weather. The agency described emergency supplies as 'insufficient,' citing months of funding shortfalls and restrictions that constrained preparations, and urged the immediate entry of winter materials plus additional funding.
items.title: OCHA warns Gaza flood victims face immediate risk amid supply shortages

items.summary: Democratic lawmakers across Europe are urging stricter regulation of AI data centres, a stance echoed continent-wide. In Amsterdam, hundreds of activists occupied the site where a planned Microsoft facility was to be built during a two-day protest spanning the region.
items.title: European Democrats Push Back on AI Data Centres Amid Protests

items.summary: BBT SE, which operates the Brenner Base Tunnel linking Austria and Italy, confirmed a cyberattack to Tiroler Tageszeitung on 07 November 2026. Local media reports suggest the Russian-speaking group Everest may be responsible, citing links to an international extortion network; ZeroFox analysis describes such groups as stealing data and demanding payment. The company said it isolated affected systems, notified authorities, and found no operational impact.
items.title: Brenner Base Tunnel Operator Hit by Suspected Russian Cyberattack

items.summary: Russian authorities said Russia launched overnight strikes on Kyiv, hitting the Northern Bridge and Meridian Plant, which they say produce Flamingo cruise missiles. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles to Russia, calling it an attempt to force a blackout. Ukrainian officials confirmed damage and one death; the attacks come days before trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.
items.title: Russia strikes Kyiv with drones and missiles ahead of talks

items.summary: Partial results from South Africa's local elections suggest coalition battles in several major cities as the once-dominant ANC is set to lose significant support, with nearly 31% of votes out of 90% counted. The DA has gained ground but remains short of its 2016 peak, while MK is contesting for the first time since forming in 2023 and may finish third nationally. Analyst Daniel Silke told AFP that complex negotiations lie ahead as parties bargain to assemble governing alliances.
items.title: South African Local Elections Point to Coalition Battles

items.summary: Former Paraguayan Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in Friday as president to finish the term of Santiago Peña, who was impeached earlier that day for misconduct in office. A unanimous vote by 44 senators removed Peña over a bank collapse tied to his government; regulators had seized Ueno Bank, affecting nearly 3 million customers three days prior. Peña is under house arrest on suspicion of breach of trust and has denied wrongdoing while prosecutors also investigate Alliana.
items.title: Paraguay's VP Alliana Sworn In After Peña Impeached

items.summary: A 75-year-old man died after a workplace incident at Regis Resources' Duketon South operation, about 130 kilometres north of Laverton and more than 700km from Perth. Emergency services were called to the Bandya mining camp on Friday, November 6, where mine staff gave first aid before he could be revived. Regis confirmed the man was part of its contract team working at the site when it occurred, and has stood down operations while investigations continue.
items.title: 75-Year-Old Miner Dies in Western Australia Goldfields Incident

items.summary: A Washington State judge approved a settlement in In re Amazon Return Policy Litigation for $309.5 million, payable to class members who bought physical items between September 5, 2017 and February 12, 2026, requested refunds that were never issued or were reversed after return. The lawsuit alleged Amazon failed to process compliant returns due to refund-process defects. Jeff Bezos' Amazon stated it is not involved in wrongdoing but agreed to avoid further litigation; the notice noted it does not express a court opinion on the merits.
items.title: Amazon Agrees to $309.5 Million Return Refund Settlement

items.summary: Elon Musk announced on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 at its facility outside Austin, Texas. The move will free capacity for the company's Cybercab robotaxi as Tesla shifts focus toward autonomous vehicles. Contributing factors include disappointing sales and pricing: Kelley Blue Book estimated 20,237 units sold last year, roughly half of the prior year, with a further 28% decline through September this year versus Musk's projected annual target of 250,000 Cybertrucks. The promised price below $40,000 never materialised; early vehicles sold for double that or more. Growing controversy around Musk and his political associations also alienated some owners. Despite the shutdown, owner Ross Blankenship said he would buy another in a heartbeat, calling its end 'a sad moment.'
items.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production in Mid-2027

items.summary: Donald Harrison, a SpaceX board member since 2015, resigned after more than a decade with the company. Bloomberg reported that independent directors are reportedly examining a potential merger between Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla, including special committees to assess a possible combination. No definitive agreement has been disclosed; efforts may target announcement in early next year.
items.title: SpaceX Board Member Donald Harrison Resigns Amid Tesla Merger Reports

items.summary: Ayodhya celebrated its 10th Deepotsav festival along the Saryu River, with millions of earthen lamps illuminating more than 30 lakh lamps across 56 ghats. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, Uttar Pradesh governor Anandiben Patel and chief minister Yogi Adityanath attended prayers before a gathering at Ram Katha Park. Adityanath called the event a symbol of Ayodhya's transformation following the Ram temple inauguration, while Patel highlighted rising tourism bringing economic opportunities to local residents.
items.title: Ayodhya lights up for Deepotsav on Diwali eve

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi said publisher Penguin Random House India was 'uneasy' with criticism of the government, in her first reaction to a controversy over an upcoming memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. In the same statement she criticised shrinking space for opposition voices under the NDA government. The report is by Aastha Jha of The Times of India.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Says Penguin Was Uneasy Over Memoir Criticism

items.summary: Divi's Laboratories reported a 64% year-on-year rise in profit after tax, reaching Rs 1,127 crore for the quarter ended September 30. Net revenue from operations climbed 35.4% to Rs 3,676 crore, up from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier. Consolidated total income rose to Rs 3,770 crore, while standalone first-half income reached Rs 6,765 crore against Rs 5,282 crore last year. The company's shares closed at Rs 10,305 on the BSE. Article author Kumar Gaurav disclosed no financial interest in the companies covered.
items.title: Divi's Laboratories Posts Strong Q2 Profit and Revenue Growth

items.summary: A controversy has emerged around Miss Universe India 2026 after second runner-up Anushri Satavlekar relinquished her position and alleged the pageant's internal practices conflicted with her values. She claimed the crown was sold and the outcome had been planned, per a NewsX Live report. Nikhil Anand, National Director of Miss India Universe and chairman of Glam Anand Group, has reportedly sought clarification from Satavlekar over the allegations. The claims remain unverified in available information.
items.title: Miss Universe India contestant alleges pageant was planned, director seeks clarification

items.summary: Bookish Review examines Devki Pande’s debut novel, The Imitation Englishman (Bloomsbury India), which offers a fresh perspective on lesser-known strands of India’s freedom struggle. Set mostly in Europe and London around 1916, the story follows 20-year-old Madhusudan heading to Heidelberg University while his brother serves as a sepoy in North Africa during the First World War. Through his friendship with Amir Farooqui, involved in the Hindu-German conspiracy, Madhusudan learns about revolutionary activity and the freedom movement at home. Pande traces social history rather than popular hagiographies, showing the struggle comprised armed revolts, collaborators and quiet subversives. The reviewer notes the plot lacks cohesion and reads as two separate stories, though it remains a fast-paced read released in October amid national protests referencing India’s freedom struggle.
items.title: Review of The Imitation Englishman by Devki Pande

items.summary:
N Chandrababu Naidu's official residence at 1, Janpath Road in New Delhi was renovated at a cost of ₹6.5 crore, reported Indian Express. The restoration, carried out by NBCC (India) Ltd over three-and-a-half months and completed on October 22, upgraded the nearly 100-year-old bungalow while preserving its architectural design and heritage elements dating to the 1930s. NBCC said it reinforced the structure through retrofitting and added modern interiors, sustainable net-zero concepts and landscaped green spaces. Naidu held housewarming rituals there in July 2024 after his election as Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, and has used the residence for official engagements with Union Ministers. The article also reports that he later visited cyclone-hit areas of Bapatla district to assess crop losses from Cyclone Murusu.

visual null},
items.title: Andhra Pradesh CM's Delhi Residence Renovated for ₹6.5 Crore

items.summary: The Indian Express reported that Mercury Public Affairs disclosed in a Foreign Agents Registration Act filing that a June social media post by President Donald Trump congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi was among tasks done for the Indian embassy’s monthly $75,000 retainer. Congress Media Coordinator Harmeet Kaur questioned what taxpayers receive from the government’s reported $225,000-a-month American lobbying spend.
items.title: Indian embassy lobbying retainer surfaces Trump congratulatory post

items.summary: Sonam Wangchuk has appealed to President Droupadi Murmu for urgent intervention, alleging that the Lieutenant Governor-led administration is running a targeted campaign to defame him and other critics. The appeal comes amid administrative action against institutions linked to him, including cancellation of Himalayan Institute of Alternatives' land lease in August 2025. Wangchuk released excerpts from what he called a sting operation implicating links with Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena's team. He also alleged restrictions on democratic rights and claimed liquor policy changes reduced mandatory No Objection Certificates from 16 to six, per PTI. The L-G's office gave no immediate response.
items.title: Climate Activist Appeals to President Over Alleged Smear Campaign in Ladakh

items.summary: Ayodhya's Deepotsav festival is set to light nearly 30 lakh traditional earthen diyas, aiming for its ninth Guinness World Record. Student volunteers and community members prepare the lamps, while officials link the event to cultural ties with Ramayana literature and urban development promoted by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath across Uttar Pradesh.
items.title: Ayodhya Lights Nearly 30 Lakh Diyas for Ninth World Record

items.summary: President Trump announced that NASA will launch its first nuclear-powered spacecraft, the Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom mission, to Mars within two years. Speaking at the UP Summit in Florida, he cited a Fox News report and linked the effort to his American Declaration of Freedom in Space. The reactor would power electric thrusters for deep-space travel.
items.title: Trump Sets Two-Year Deadline for NASA Nuclear Mars Mission

items.summary: Police say a 15-year-old boy killed his 58-year-old father at their home in Loni early Saturday after being scolded for fighting with his younger sister. The incident occurred between 2am and 3am while the family slept, according to police. ACP Ram Kishan of Loni Circle told HT that the boy attacked him with a sickle; other relatives then apprehended him and took him to a hospital where he was declared dead.
items.title: Teenager Kills Father After Being Scolded Over Fight With Sister in Loni

items.summary: Writer Perumal Murugan has accused the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore of serious procurement irregularities, including AI-generated content, fictitious authors and inflated prices. In an article on Sindhai dated November 6, he counted nearly 1,800 books bearing the imprint of Agalvilakku Pathippagam and more than 100 titles from Phoenix Pathippagam. He cited a Rs 1,445 price tag versus comparable copies at approximately Rs 350, plus historical errors such as misattributing Naladiyar to an individual poet. Tamil Nadu School Education Minister A Rajmohan said about 1,500 books were purchased during the previous DMK administration and filed a complaint with DVAC on November 7. The ruling TVK blames the former DMK government; both parties demand investigations as the outcome remains awaited.
items.title: Tamil Writer Accuses Coimbatore Library of AI-Generated Books and Fake Authors

items.summary: A former regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region, Paramjith Dhankhar, was shot dead on Friday night by his neighbour Mohan Sharma over a parking dispute that had strained the two families for days. The feud also involved Sharma’s son allegedly using his dog to defecate in the shared area. Police said nine of at least 15 fired bullets hit Dhankhar, whose body went to Badshah Khan Civil Hospital for autopsy; Sharma has since been arrested (PTI).
items.title: Neighbour Shoots Former Tech Mahindra Executive Over Parking Feud in Faridabad

items.summary: Congress chairperson Sonia Gandhi said publisher Penguin Random House India declined her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love because it was uneasy with criticism of the government. She called the refusal an attempt to censor her book and described being disappointed but not surprised. The Guardian reported her comments ahead of a November 10 release; HarperCollins India then agreed to publish it domestically that same day.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Blames Penguin for Memoir Withdrawal, Calls It Censorship

items.summary: Websol Energy System reported second-quarter FY27 results via an exchange filing. Revenue from operations rose 114.6% YoY to Rs 361.02 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs 168.22 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA climbed 77.3% to Rs 128.14 crore from Rs 72.29 crore. Cell production reached 255 MW at 91% utilisation, module output was 88 MW at 68%, and the order book stood at Rs 1,280 crore as of September 30, 2026. Managing Director Sohan Lal Agarwal said the quarter showed manufacturing progress while preparing for expansion into EPC, solar IPP and energy trading.
items.title: Websol Energy Q2 Results: PAT jumps 73% YoY to Rs 80 crore; revenue more than doubles to Rs 361 crore

items.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum gained roughly 0.6% and 0.8% over the past 24 hours, while BNB, Solana, Hyperliquid, Dogecoin and Cardano rose up to 1.8%. ZebPay's Harish Vatnani said crypto stayed under pressure after the Binance security incident, heavy ETF outflows and a US tech sell-off outweighed a post-election rally; sentiment swung back into fear as the Fear & Greed Index fell from 50 to 28 and market capitalisation slipped to about $2.6 trillion. BTC is now about 40% below its October all-time high of around $126,000 and trades just above the $75,000 support level.
items.title: Crypto Markets Rise as Jobs Data Weighs on Bitcoin

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging him to withhold all statutory and administrative clearances for Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu dam project until co-basin states consent, citing concerns over the reported 67.16 TMC reservoir capacity across the Cauvery River. In a letter dated November 6, Vijay argued that the project would disrupt water flows and monthly deliveries to Tamil Nadu as mandated by the Supreme Court, fueling anxiety among farmers amid the deficit year 2026-27. He referenced earlier legal actions, including an NGT application filed on May 27 and a June 19 Assembly resolution, while requesting deferral of site inspections and technical evaluations pending inter-State resolution.
items.title: Tamil Nadu CM Urges Modi to Block Mekedatu Clearances Without Consent

items.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Kumar Choudhary questioned the Centre's appointment of Dr. Sajjan Singh Yadav, a 1995-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre transferred from Delhi, as the new Union Territory's Chief Secretary. Choudhary argued that J&K should have been represented by one of its own senior officers following the October 31 retirement of outgoing incumbent Atal Dulloo, a Kashmiri Pandit he said was not granted an extension or replaced locally. Yadav is scheduled to assume charge from November 1, with Additional Chief Secretary Shaleen Kabra currently officiating. Choudhary clarified his demand concerned local representation across the administrative hierarchy rather than any religion or region.
items.title: J&K Deputy CM Questions Outsider Chief Secretary Appointment

items.summary: On Friday night, a 32-year-old woman was rescued after allegedly jumping into Talaopali Lake near the boating centre and Precision Fisheries in Thane West. A distress call arrived around 9.22 pm on November 6. Disaster Management Officer Y.M. Tadvi coordinated personnel from the Disaster Response Force, which used a boat to bring her out safely. Officials confirmed she sustained no injuries.
items.title: Woman Rescued After Allegedly Jumping Into Talaopali Lake in Thane West

items.summary: Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee launched a scathing attack on the BJP, alleging hooliganism by a gang of thugs who disrupted Kali Puja celebrations in Kolkata's Kalighat area. She said the disturbance was deliberate and blamed it on revoked permissions for traditional pujas while new ones were allowed on the main road. Speaking to reporters she challenged the party: 'If you have the courage to use a bulldozer, why do you come here at 3:00 in the morning with a gang of thugs?' She ended by telling them to run their bulldozers over her and her people.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee rails against BJP after Kalighat Kali Puja disruption
